segments.text: X seventeen is the First Napoleon Point of triangle A B C: by Napoleon's theorem, the centroids Nap sub a, Nap sub b, and Nap sub c of the three outward equilateral triangles erected on sides B C, C A, and A B always form an equilateral triangle, and the lines joining A, B, and C to those three centers concur at X seventeen.
